_publications: Structure, section order and entry numbering follow the Foundation's publications document. Entry data follows the import sheet, which carries the verified corrections; the five internet-article links come from the document, which kept them where the sheet left them empty.

database.lede: Everything Dr. Ingham published, verified against its source and linked. Corrections welcome at info@soilfoodweb.com.
notes: 55 entries have no source link. Links or PDFs where they exist. Linnea and Evan.

the five internet articles carry links from the old page that were not re-verified, and one of them (the 2015 carbon sequestration piece) is from Mercola.com and was recommended for removal. Decide before launch. Evan.
the Klebsiella planticola entry merges two entries from the old page and has a public controversy history. Attribution under review. Evan and Alex.
the corrections sheet (49 places the new list differs from the old page, each with its reason) is not published anywhere yet. Decide whether it goes on this page. Linnea.

columnNote.h3: Monthly column in BioCycle, about 1998 to 2000
columnNote.body: Monthly column including discussions of: Anaerobic Bacteria and Composting, The Good, the Bad and Facultative Anaerobes, What Organisms are in Compost?, What is Compost Tea?, Methyl Bromide Alternatives, Fungi and Disease-Suppression, Vermicompost versus Compost, What’s the Difference?
columnNote.after: Numerous other magazine and newspaper publications since 1999.

database.counts: 180 publications. 166 link to the publisher record, Google Scholar or a repository copy; 14 are listed by citation because no copy was found online.

facets.name: Organisms
facets.about: the groups Soil Food Web students learn to identify under the microscope

tags.definition: studies that measure, count or manipulate soil or compost bacteria.
studies of soil fungi, fungal hyphae or fungal biomass, including fungal plant pathogens.
fungi that live in partnership with plant roots (arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal).
flagellates, amoebae and ciliates, the main grazers of bacteria.
beneficial and root-feeding nematodes.
mites, springtails, symphylans and other small soil animals.
earthworms, including the worms used to make vermicompost.

facets.name: Practices and inputs
facets.about: what a grower or land manager actually does

tags.definition: making, testing or applying thermal compost.
brewed compost tea and water extracts of compost or vermicompost, used as a drench or foliar spray.
worm castings and vermicompost as an input.
cover crops, no-till, reduced tillage, crop rotation and alley cropping.
the effects of biocides, fungicides, antibiotics and soil fumigants on soil life.
genetically engineered organisms released into soil, and their regulation.
nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur cycling, mineralization and nitrogen fixation.
carbon storage, carbon sequestration and soil CO2 flux.
breakdown of litter, logs and other organic matter.
biological control of plant diseases, including induced plant resistance.
biological control of insect and other plant pests.
measured plant growth, seedling vigour or crop yield.
nutritional quality of crops, milk and other food.
cleaning up contaminated soil or water, including heavy metals and hazardous waste sites.

facets.name: Systems
facets.about: the kind of land the study was done on

tags.definition: field crops, vegetables, orchards and dairy farms.
container growing, greenhouses, nurseries, turf and ornamentals.
conifer, deciduous and riparian forests, and forest restoration.
prairie, meadow and rangeland.
wetlands and stream-side soils.
soil life under snow and in the non-growing season.
studies of the food web as a whole: who eats whom and what that does for plants.
methods for counting, staining and measuring soil organisms.
the diversity of soil organisms and why it matters.
regulation, policy and soil as a matter of public concern.
papers that review or summarize a body of research.
done outdoors on real farms, forests or rangeland.
plants grown in pots or containers under controlled conditions.
done in the lab, in petri dishes, microcosms or cultures.
summarizes earlier research.
describes or tests a way to measure something.
technical reports, manuals and handbooks.
magazine columns, newsletters, opinion pieces and internet articles.

region.note: Region is where the study was done. Global means a review, a multi-country study, or work that is about no particular place.

entries.title: Ultraviolet-induced autofluorescence of arbuscular mycorrhizal root infections: An alternative to clearing and staining methods for assessing infections
entries.authors: Ames, R.N., E.R. Ingham and C.P.P. Reid
entries.summary: Tests UV light under a fluorescence microscope as a way to see arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in untreated roots, across five plant families, as an alternative to clearing and staining.
entries.useful_for: Lab techs and students of soil microscopy, to learn a faster way to check whether roots are colonized by mycorrhizal fungi.

entries.title: Ultraviolet-induced autofluorescence: a new method for detecting and quantifying vesicular-arbuscular mycorrhizal root infections
entries.authors: Ames, R.N., E.R. Ingham and C.P.P. Reid
entries.summary: A short conference report introducing the UV autofluorescence method for detecting and counting vesicular-arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in roots.
entries.useful_for: Readers interested in the history of root microscopy, to see the first announcement of the UV method for spotting mycorrhizal fungi.

entries.title: Relationship between fluorescein diacetate-stained hyphae and oxygen utilization, glucose utilization and biomass of submerged fungal batch cultures
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and D.A. Klein
entries.summary: Compares FDA staining of fungal strands with oxygen use, glucose use and biomass in fungal cultures, to test whether the stain marks active fungi.
entries.useful_for: Students of soil microscopy, to learn the research behind telling active fungi apart from total fungi on a soil report.

entries.title: The effect of chloroform on protozoa and other soil inhabitants
entries.authors: McClellan, J.F., D.C. Coleman, K.A. Horton and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Reports how chloroform fumigation, a common lab step for estimating soil microbial biomass, affects protozoa and other soil organisms.
entries.useful_for: Consultants and lab techs, to understand why fumigation-based lab tests and direct microscope counts can give different pictures of soil life.

entries.title: Soil fungi: Relationships between hyphal activity and staining with fluorescein diacetate
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and D.A. Klein
entries.summary: Compares FDA staining with measures of fungal activity in soil and examines how well the stain reflects living, active fungi.
entries.useful_for: Lab techs doing soil microscopy, to see the evidence behind the active fungal numbers they report to clients.

entries.title: Soil fungi: Measurement of hyphal length
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and D.A. Klein
entries.summary: Describes a method for measuring the length of fungal strands in soil samples, a step in calculating fungal biomass.
entries.useful_for: Anyone who reads soil food web reports, to learn how the fungal biomass number is built up from strand length.

entries.title: Rhizosphere bacterial population responses to root colonization by a vesicular-arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus
entries.authors: Ames, R.N., C.P.P. Reid and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Reports changes in bacterial populations around roots after the roots were colonized by a vesicular-arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus.
entries.useful_for: Growers using mycorrhizal inoculants, to see how adding one beneficial fungus may shift the bacteria living around their plant roots.

entries.title: Phosphatase activity of Penicillium citrinum submerged batch cultures and its relationship to fungal activity
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and D.A. Klein
entries.summary: Measures phosphatase enzyme activity in cultures of the soil fungus Penicillium citrinum and relates it to how active the fungus is.
entries.useful_for: Farmers aiming to cut phosphorus fertiliser, to learn how fungal enzymes help release phosphorus that is already in the soil.

entries.title: Effects of streptomycin, cycloheximide, fungizone, captan, carbofuran, cygon and PCNB on soil microbe populations and nutrient cycling
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and D.C. Coleman
entries.summary: Tests seven pesticides and fungicides, including captan, carbofuran and PCNB, on soil microbe populations and nutrient cycling.
entries.useful_for: Farmers deciding whether to spray, to weigh early evidence on how common chemicals affect the microbes that cycle nutrients for their crops.

entries.title: Interactions of bacteria, fungi and their nematode grazers: Effects on nutrient cycling and plant growth
entries.authors: Ingham, R.E., J.A. Trofymow, E.R. Ingham and D.C. Coleman
entries.summary: Grows plants in soil with bacteria, fungi and the nematodes that graze on them, and reports that nematode grazing increased nitrogen available to plants and plant growth.
entries.useful_for: Students of the Soil Food Web approach, to read the study behind the idea that predators of microbes release nutrients for plants.

entries.title: Review of the effects of twelve selected biocides on target and non-target soil organisms
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: Reviews published research on twelve biocides and their effects on both target organisms and other soil organisms.
entries.useful_for: Farmers and advisors moving away from chemical inputs, to find one reference that gathers evidence on side effects in soil.

entries.title: Responses of microbial components of the rhizosphere to plant management strategies in a semiarid rangeland
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., D.A. Klein and M.J. Trlica
entries.summary: Compares microbes in the root zone under different plant management strategies on semiarid rangeland.
entries.useful_for: Ranchers and land managers on dry grazing land, to see how management choices may change the life around plant roots.

entries.title: Manipulation of bacteria, fungi and protozoa by biocides in lodgepole pine forest soil microcosms: Effects on organism interactions and nitrogen mineralization
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., C. Cambardella and D.C. Coleman
entries.summary: Uses biocides to remove bacteria, fungi or protozoa from lodgepole pine forest soil in microcosms and tracks the effects on organism interactions and nitrogen release.
entries.useful_for: Students of soil ecology, to learn what each major organism group contributes to the nitrogen that plants depend on.

entries.title: Filter-out grazers (FOG): A filtration experiment for separating protozoan grazers in soil
entries.authors: Frey, J.S., J.F. McClellan, E.R. Ingham and D.C. Coleman
entries.summary: Describes a filtration method that separates protozoa from other soil organisms so their grazing effects can be studied on their own.
entries.useful_for: Researchers and advanced students, to learn a lab technique for isolating protozoa in experiments.

entries.title: Trophic interactions and nitrogen cycling in a semiarid grassland soil. Part I. Seasonal dynamics of the natural populations, their interactions and effects on nitrogen cycling
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., J.A. Trofymow, R.N. Ames, H.W. Hunt, C.R. Morley, J.C. Moore and D.C. Coleman
entries.summary: Follows natural populations of soil organisms through the seasons in a semiarid grassland and links their feeding interactions to nitrogen cycling.
entries.useful_for: Growers planning when to add compost or extracts, to understand how soil life and nutrient release change through the year.

entries.title: Trophic interactions and nitrogen cycling in a semiarid grassland soil. Part II. System responses to removal of different groups of soil microbes or fauna
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., J.A. Trofymow, R.N. Ames, H.W. Hunt, C.R. Morley, J.C. Moore and D.C. Coleman
entries.summary: Removes different groups of soil microbes or animals from grassland soil and measures how nitrogen cycling responds in the remaining system.
entries.useful_for: Students and consultants, to see experimental support for why a complete soil food web helps supply plant nutrients.

entries.title: The detrital food web in a short grass prairie
entries.authors: Hunt, H.W., D.C. Coleman, E.R. Ingham, R.E. Ingham, E.T. Elliott, J.C. Moore, C.P.P. Reid and C.R. Morley
entries.summary: Builds a food web model of the organisms that break down dead plant material in a shortgrass prairie and estimates nitrogen flow through each group.
entries.useful_for: Anyone learning the Soil Food Web approach, to study the classic food web diagram that much of the field builds on.

entries.title: Inter- and intraspecific feeding selectivity of Folsomia candida (Willem) (Collembola, Isotomidae) on fungi: Method development and ecological consequences
entries.authors: Moore, J.C., E.R. Ingham and D.C. Coleman
entries.summary: Tests which fungi the springtail Folsomia candida chooses to eat and develops a method for measuring these feeding preferences.
entries.useful_for: Students of soil ecology, to learn how small soil animals may influence which fungi grow in a soil.

entries.title: Bacterial, fungal and protozoan responses to chloroform fumigation in stored prairie soil
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and K.A. Horton
entries.summary: Measures how bacteria, fungi and protozoa in stored prairie soil respond to chloroform fumigation.
entries.useful_for: Lab techs and researchers, to read fumigation-based biomass results with the right caution.

entries.title: Carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur cycling in terrestrial ecosystems
entries.authors: Coleman, D.C. and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: An introduction to a journal issue on how carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur move through land ecosystems.
entries.useful_for: Students new to soil science, to get a compact overview of the nutrient cycles that soil organisms help drive.

entries.title: Nitrogen limitation of production and decomposition in prairie, mountain meadow, and pine forest
entries.authors: Hunt, H.W., E.R. Ingham, D.C. Coleman, E.T. Elliott and C.P.P. Reid
entries.summary: Compares prairie, mountain meadow and pine forest to examine how nitrogen supply limits plant production and decomposition.
entries.useful_for: Land managers, to understand why plant growth and decomposition may slow where nitrogen is scarce.

entries.title: Early patterns of heterotroph activity in conifer logs
entries.authors: Carpenter, S.E., M.E. Harmon, E.R. Ingham, R.G. Kelsey, J.D. Lattin and T.D. Schowalter
entries.summary: Follows the early activity of fungi, bacteria and insects that colonize and begin decomposing fallen conifer logs.
entries.useful_for: Foresters and anyone managing woody debris, to learn how the breakdown of fallen wood begins.

entries.title: Social and economic concerns with respect to the choice of critical terrestrial ecosystems
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., M.V. Wilson and C.D. McIntire
entries.summary: A U.S. EPA report discussing the social and economic factors in choosing which land ecosystems to treat as critical for protection.
entries.useful_for: Readers working on soil and land policy, to see how science and social priorities meet when deciding which land to protect.

entries.title: Interactions between soil animals and ectomycorrhizal fungal mats
entries.authors: Cromack, K., Jr., B.L. Fichter, A.M. Moldenke, J.A. Entry and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Studies how soil animals interact with dense mats of ectomycorrhizal fungi in forest soils.
entries.useful_for: Foresters, to learn about fungal mats, hotspots of soil life that help forest trees take up nutrients.

entries.title: An analysis of food-web structure and function in a shortgrass prairie, a mountain meadow, and a lodgepole pine forest
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., D.C. Coleman and J.C. Moore
entries.summary: Compares the structure and function of soil food webs in a shortgrass prairie, a mountain meadow and a lodgepole pine forest.
entries.useful_for: Growers and consultants, to learn why the target fungal to bacterial balance may depend on the plants being grown.

entries.title: Use of staining and inhibitors to separate fungal and bacterial activity in soil
entries.authors: Stamatiadis, S., J.W. Doran and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Tests stains and chemical inhibitors as a way to separate fungal activity from bacterial activity in soil samples.
entries.useful_for: Lab techs and students, to learn methods behind measuring the fungal to bacterial balance.

entries.title: Seasonal and faunal effects on decomposition in semiarid prairie, meadow and lodgepole pine forest
entries.authors: Coleman, D.C., E.R. Ingham, H.W. Hunt, E.T. Elliott, C.P.P. Reid and J.C. Moore
entries.summary: Compares decomposition in prairie, meadow and pine forest across seasons, with and without soil animals present.
entries.useful_for: Growers building organic matter, to see how soil animals may affect how fast plant residues break down.

entries.title: Comparison of direct versus fumigation incubation microbial biomass estimates in ectomycorrhizal mat and non-mat soils
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., R. Griffiths, K. Cromack and J.A. Entry
entries.summary: Compares direct microscope counts with the fumigation-incubation method for estimating microbial biomass in soils with and without fungal mats.
entries.useful_for: Anyone choosing a soil test, to understand why different lab methods may give different microbial numbers.

entries.title: A comparison of agar film techniques for estimating fungal biovolumes in litter and soil
entries.authors: Lodge, D.J. and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Compares agar film techniques for estimating how much fungus is present in leaf litter and soil.
entries.useful_for: Lab techs and students of soil microscopy, to compare the direct methods used to measure fungi.

entries.title: Microbial characteristics of ectomycorrhizal mat communities in Oregon and California
entries.authors: Griffiths, R.P., E.R. Ingham, B.A. Caldwell, M.A. Castellano and K. Cromack, Jr.
entries.summary: Describes the microbial characteristics of ectomycorrhizal fungal mat communities in forests in Oregon and California.
entries.useful_for: Foresters and researchers, to get a detailed look at the microbes in these forest soil hotspots.

entries.title: Reduction of microbial and faunal groups following application of streptomycin and captan in Georgia no-tillage agroecosystems
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., D.C. Coleman, R. Parmelee and D.A. Crossley
entries.summary: Reports reductions in microbial and soil animal groups after the antibiotic streptomycin and the fungicide captan were applied to no-tillage fields in Georgia.
entries.useful_for: No-till farmers, to see evidence that chemical inputs may reduce soil life even after tillage has stopped.

entries.title: Decomposition of fallen trees: Effects of initial conditions and heterotroph colonization rates
entries.authors: Schowalter, T.D., B.A. Caldwell, S.E. Carpenter, R.P. Griffiths, M.E. Harmon, E.R. Ingham, R.G. Kelsey, J.D. Lattin and A.R. Moldenke
entries.citation: Pages 373-383 in K.P. Singh and J.S. Singh (eds), Tropical Ecosystems: Ecology and Management. Wiley Eastern, New Delhi
entries.summary: Examines how the starting condition of fallen trees and the rate at which organisms colonize them affect decomposition.
entries.useful_for: Foresters, to learn which factors influence how quickly fallen trees return nutrients to the soil.

entries.title: The functional significance and regulation of soil biodiversity: An executive summary of the Soil Ecology Society meeting
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: A newsletter summary of a Soil Ecology Society meeting on the functional importance of soil biodiversity and what regulates it.
entries.useful_for: Newcomers to soil ecology, to get a short overview of why researchers consider soil biodiversity important.

entries.title: The sustainable biosphere initiative: A commentary from the U.S. Soil Ecology Society
entries.authors: Klopatek, C.C., E.G. O'Neill, D.W. Freckman, C.D. Bledsoe, D.A. Coleman, D.A. Crossley, Jr., E.R. Ingham, D. Parkinson and J.M. Klopatek
entries.citation: Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America, 73:223-228
entries.summary: A commentary from the U.S. Soil Ecology Society on how soil ecology research should fit into a national agenda for a sustainable biosphere.
entries.useful_for: Readers working on soil policy, to see how soil scientists argued for including soil life in sustainability planning.

entries.title: Population responses of target and non-target forest-soil organisms to selected biocides
entries.authors: Colinas, C., E. Ingham and R. Molina
entries.summary: Tests how target and non-target organisms in forest soil respond to selected biocides.
entries.useful_for: Foresters weighing chemical treatments, to review evidence on effects beyond the intended targets.

entries.title: Soil organisms and forest health
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: A general-audience article on the roles soil organisms play in keeping forests healthy.
entries.useful_for: Readers without a science background, to get an accessible introduction to forest soil life.

entries.title: Use of sulfamethoxazole-penicillin, oxytetracycline, carbofuran, carbaryl, naphthalene and Temik to remove key organism groups in soil in a corn agroecosystem
entries.authors: Coleman, D.C., D.A. Crossley, Jr. and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Uses specific antibiotics and pesticides to remove key organism groups from soil in a corn field and tracks the effects.
entries.useful_for: Crop farmers, to learn what different soil organism groups may contribute in a working field.

entries.title: Protozoan communities around conifer roots colonized by ectomycorrhizal fungi
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and H. Massicotte
entries.summary: Describes protozoan communities in the soil around conifer roots colonized by ectomycorrhizal fungi.
entries.useful_for: Students of soil ecology, to learn how protozoa fit into the root zone food web that helps feed trees.

entries.title: Assessing interactions between the soil foodweb and a strain of Pseudomonas putida genetically engineered to degrade 2,4-D
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R., J.D. Doyle and C.W. Hendricks
entries.summary: Tests interactions between the soil food web and a Pseudomonas putida strain genetically engineered to break down the herbicide 2,4-D.
entries.useful_for: Readers following debates on engineered microbes, to see an early study of their possible effects on soil life.

entries.title: Soil protozoa
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: A short review of a book on soil protozoa, discussing their role in food webs and nitrogen release.
entries.useful_for: Students, to get a brief introduction to the single-celled grazers that release nutrients from bacteria.

entries.title: Foundations of biodiversity in managed Douglas-fir forests
entries.authors: Carey, A.B., D.R. Thysell, L.J. Villa, T.M. Wilson, S.M. Wilson, J.M. Trappe, W. Colgan, E.R. Ingham and M. Holmes
entries.citation: In: Peterson, D.L. and C.V. Klimas (eds), The role of restoration in the ecosystem. Proceedings of the 2nd Symposium for Ecological Restoration. Madison, WI: Society for Ecological Restoration, 68-82
entries.summary: Describes a study on managing second-growth Douglas-fir forests to develop the biodiversity of older forests, including soil organisms.
entries.useful_for: Forest managers, to learn approaches for building biodiversity back into managed forests.

entries.title: Responses of soil foodweb organisms in the first year following clearcutting and application of chloropicrin to control laminated root rot
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and W.G. Thies
entries.summary: Compares soil food web organisms in a clearcut and an uncut Douglas-fir forest, and after chloropicrin was applied to stumps, reporting large drops in fungal biomass within a year.
entries.useful_for: Foresters planning replanting after root rot, to understand how clearcutting and fumigation may set back soil life.

entries.title: Soil biology and ecology
entries.authors: Rygiewicz, P.T. and E.R. Ingham
entries.citation: In Fairbridge, R.W. and D.E. Alexander (eds), Encyclopedia of Environmental Science. Van Nostrand Reinhold, NY
entries.summary: An encyclopedia entry giving an overview of soil biology and ecology.
entries.useful_for: Students new to soil biology, to get a short reference overview of the field.

entries.title: Conventional and organic alternatives to methyl bromide on California strawberries: Effect of Brassica residues and spent mushroom compost following successive chemical fumigation
entries.authors: Sances, F.V. and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Compares methyl bromide with chemical and organic alternatives, including broccoli residues and mushroom compost, in a commercial California strawberry field.
entries.useful_for: Strawberry and vegetable growers, to see early field data on biological alternatives to soil fumigation, including the trade-offs in weeds and yield.

entries.title: Chemistry and microbial activity of forest and pasture riparian-zone soils along three Pacific Northwest streams
entries.authors: Griffiths, R.P., J.A. Entry, E.R. Ingham and W.H. Emmingham
entries.summary: Compares forest and pasture soils along three Pacific Northwest streams and reports more carbon, nutrients and fungal biomass in the forest soils.
entries.useful_for: Farmers and land managers near streams, to see evidence on how forested buffer strips may protect water quality.

entries.title: Changes in rhizosphere microflora and microfauna 10 years following Douglas-fir live tree injection with chloropicrin or methylisothiocyanate
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and W. Thies
entries.summary: Measures root zone microbes and microfauna ten years after Douglas-fir trees were injected with chloropicrin or methylisothiocyanate.
entries.useful_for: Foresters, to learn how long the effects of fumigant injection may last in soil.

entries.title: Soil foodweb structure and function in forests: A comparison of conifer, deciduous, riparian and managed forests
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.citation: Proceedings of the IUFRO Interdisciplinary Uneven-aged Management Symposium
entries.summary: Compares soil food web structure and function in conifer, deciduous, riparian and managed forests.
entries.useful_for: Foresters and consultants, to match soil biology goals to the type of forest.

entries.title: Foodweb methodology to assess ecological effects of anthropogenic stressors in soil
entries.authors: Hendricks, C.W., M.T. Holmes and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: Describes how soil food web measurements can be used to detect the ecological effects of pollution and other human stresses on soil.
entries.useful_for: Environmental consultants, to learn how soil life can serve as an indicator of soil damage.

entries.title: Ectomycorrhizae establishment on Douglas-fir seedlings following chloropicrin treatment to control laminated-root rot disease: Assessment 4 and 5 years after outplanting
entries.authors: Massicotte, H.B., L.E. Tackaberry, E.R. Ingham and W.G. Thies
entries.summary: Assesses ectomycorrhizal fungi on Douglas-fir seedlings four and five years after soil was treated with chloropicrin to control laminated root rot.
entries.useful_for: Tree nurseries and replanting crews, to see whether mycorrhizal partners return after fumigation.

entries.title: Sustainable agriculture and the ecology of soil
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and J. Barlow
entries.citation: Perspectives on Business and Global Change, 12:31-42
entries.summary: A paper for a business and policy audience on the links between soil ecology and sustainable agriculture.
entries.useful_for: Readers making the case for regenerative farming to investors or policymakers, to find arguments framed for that audience.

entries.title: Soil organisms and their role in healthy turf
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: A trade magazine article for turf managers explaining how soil organisms supply nutrients and support healthy turf.
entries.useful_for: Turf and golf course managers, to understand how a living soil can reduce their reliance on fertiliser.

entries.title: Soil view: Anaerobic bacteria and compost tea
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: A short magazine column on why anaerobic bacteria can appear in compost tea and why that matters.
entries.useful_for: Compost tea brewers, to understand why keeping tea well aerated matters for the organisms in it.

entries.title: Effects of Klebsiella planticola SDF20 on soil biota and wheat growth in sandy soil
entries.authors: Holmes, M.T., E.R. Ingham, J.D. Doyle and C.W. Hendricks
entries.summary: Adds a genetically engineered Klebsiella planticola strain to sandy soil with wheat and reports changes in nematodes that coincided with the death of the wheat plants.
entries.useful_for: Readers following debates on engineered microbes, to read a widely cited study on their possible risks to crops and soil life.

entries.title: The mycorrhizal colonization of six wetland plant species at sites differing in land use history
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R. and M.V. Wilson
entries.summary: Measures mycorrhizal colonization in six wetland plant species at sites with different histories of land use.
entries.useful_for: People restoring wetlands, to learn how past land use may affect plant partnerships with fungi.

entries.title: Dynamics of soil fungal and bacterial biomass in a temperate climate alley cropping system
entries.authors: Seiter, S., E.R. Ingham and R.D. William
entries.summary: Tracks fungal and bacterial biomass over time in an alley cropping system where crops grow between rows of trees.
entries.useful_for: Agroforestry farmers, to see how trees in crop fields may shift the soil's fungal to bacterial balance.

entries.title: Compost tea, Part I & II
entries.authors: Ingham, E.
entries.summary: A two-part magazine series by Dr. Ingham on what compost tea is and how to make it.
entries.useful_for: Gardeners and growers starting out with compost tea, to get a practical introduction from Dr. Ingham.

entries.title: The Soil Biology Primer, Chapters 1-5: The Soil Foodweb; Soil Bacteria; Soil Fungi; Soil Protozoa; Soil Nematodes
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: The USDA Soil Biology Primer, a free illustrated guide to the soil food web, bacteria, fungi, protozoa and nematodes.
entries.useful_for: Anyone new to soil biology, to get a clear, free introduction to the organisms covered in SFW courses.

entries.title: Soil biology and ecology
entries.authors: Rygiewicz, P.T. and E.R. Ingham
entries.summary: An encyclopedia entry giving an overview of soil biology and ecology.
entries.useful_for: Students new to soil biology, to get a short reference overview of the field.

entries.title: Brewing compost tea
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.summary: A gardening magazine article explaining how to brew compost tea and use it as a foliar spray or soil drench.
entries.useful_for: Home gardeners, to learn the basics of brewing and applying compost tea.

entries.title: The Compost Tea Brewing Manual
entries.authors: Ingham, E.R.
entries.citation: Sustainable Studies Institute, Eugene, OR. 60 pp.
